Overall explanation, cause and effect: raising the average heat-addition temperature through (1) high-temperature, high-pressure steam and (3) reheat improves Rankine-cycle efficiency. (2) Higher condenser vacuum lowers the exhaust pressure and saturation temperature, which lowers the heat-rejection temperature. (5) The economizer recovers exhaust-gas heat, lowering exhaust loss and raising boiler efficiency. These are all standard statements and correct.

Reason (4) is wrong: in the regenerative cycle, a feedwater heater uses extracted steam as its heat source to raise the feedwater temperature. The extracted steam gives up heat and condenses. So the claim that it "raises the extraction temperature" reverses the direction of heat flow, and it cannot be an efficiency-improvement method. Both the overall explanation and choiceExplanations[4] give this reason consistently.

Each choice has its own specific reason. (1): higher average heat-addition temperature. (2): lower exhaust pressure and saturation temperature, so lower heat-rejection temperature. (3): reheating HP turbine exhaust raises the average heat-addition temperature and reduces exhaust wetness. (5): exhaust-gas heat recovery reduces exhaust loss. None of them contradicts the correct choice. Choice (3)'s description as "high-pressure exhaust → low-pressure turbine" is a simplification commonly used at the 3rd-class level and is not an error.
